sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Band Theory**: Conductivity is determined by the **Energy Band Gap** between the Valence Band and Conduction Band. Semiconductors have a small gap (~1 eV).
• **Intrinsic Semiconductors**: Pure form (e.g., Silicon, Germanium) with no impurities; conductivity is low and temperature-dependent.
• **Extrinsic Semiconductors**: Created by **Doping** (adding impurities) to increase conductivity. Divided into **n-type** (excess electrons) and **p-type** (excess holes).
• **Key Metric**: **Fermi Level** position shifts based on doping concentration, dictating the material's electrical behavior.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Doped with Pentavalent atoms (Phosphorus, Arsenic). Excess electrons.
Doped with Trivalent atoms (Boron, Gallium). Excess holes.
Majority charge carriers are holes (positive charge).

items.definition: The intentional introduction of impurities into an intrinsic semiconductor to change its electrical properties.
The interface between p-type and n-type materials; acts as a one-way valve for current, forming the basis of all modern electronics.

items.title: Major Applications & Initiatives
items.content:
• **Applications**: Integrated Circuits (ICs), Solar Cells (Photovoltaics), LEDs, and Microprocessors.
• **Initiatives**: India Semiconductor Mission (ISM) under MeitY, focusing on Fab units and Display Fabs.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Challenges**: High capital intensity, dependence on rare earth elements, and complex supply chain geopolitics.
• **Solutions**: Focus on R&D in Compound Semiconductors (GaN, SiC) and indigenous design (PLI schemes).

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'P-B-T' and 'N-P-E'.
• **Decoded Meaning**: P-type uses Boron (Trivalent); N-type uses Phosphorus (Pentavalent/Electron-rich).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses 'Intrinsic' with 'Extrinsic'. Remember: Intrinsic = Pure (No doping); Extrinsic = Doped (Impure).
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Silicon-based economy' to describe the strategic shift in global manufacturing and India's 'Atmanirbhar' push in electronics.

keyTakeaways: Semiconductors are the backbone of the digital economy.
Doping is the mechanism that transforms insulators into functional electronic components.
India's strategic focus is on moving up the value chain from assembly to fabrication.
